The 946 preserved DOIs are explicitly acknowledged. Verification methodology included so any reader can independently confirm each claim by direct API query. Two refinements: (1) front-loaded one-paragraph summary of the thesis (OpenAIRE in writing promises persistent identification while verifiably breaking metadata for 871 specific DOIs) so readers reach the core concern immediately; (2) renamed companion paper reference from "DOIs ≠ Permanent Identifiers" to "DOIs ≠ Persistent Identifiers" — anchors the critique directly to DOIs' own self-presentation as 'persistent identifiers' rather than the looser "permanent" framing. The paper #868 has also been renamed corpus-wide for consistency.

description:
This documentary record preserves the correspondence underlying #875. It contains an initial inquiry sent by Lee Sharks on June 19, an OpenAIRE helpdesk response received June 22, and a substantially developed follow-up drafted on June 22.

The first message reports the immediate post-termination estimate and asks OpenAIRE about Zenodo’s action. The response states that CERN independently governs Zenodo and that OpenAIRE cannot access or change its moderation decisions. The third message accepts that boundary and redirects the question toward OpenAIRE’s own persistence language and metadata architecture.

The follow-up is the record’s most extensive component. It reconciles preliminary and audited counts, distinguishes 871 unavailable DataCite API records from 946 preserved records, describes concept/version correlation, supplies a verification method, inventories five OpenAIRE statements, and asks how public persistence claims relate to downstream handling of absent upstream metadata.

The title and front matter call this a verbatim three-message exchange, but the preservation notice and message header say the third item was **transmission pending at the moment of deposit**. It is therefore not evidence of a three-message exchange unless later delivery documentation exists. The accurate description is two-message correspondence plus a versioned draft follow-up.

Versions 1.1 and 1.2 refined the third message’s numbers, terminology, and front-loaded summary. Those changes are compatible with a draft, but not with a claim that the entire deposited thread is an unaltered historical exchange. The first two messages may be preserved verbatim; the third is an authored and revised document.

**OpenAIRE Helpdesk Exchange — Documentary Thread for #875** is a correspondence record by Lee Sharks.

It preserves an inquiry to OpenAIRE, the helpdesk’s reply about independent Zenodo governance, and a detailed follow-up drafted in response.

The follow-up narrows the issue to OpenAIRE’s own persistence statements and metadata architecture and uses the corrected 871/946 DataCite audit.

At deposit time, transmission of the third message was pending. The record is therefore two exchanged messages plus a revised draft unless later evidence confirms it was sent.
